# teams app update

Update a Teams app's properties

## Usage

```
teams app update [appId] [options]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `appId` | App ID | No |

## Options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--endpoint <url>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the messaging endpoint URL |
| `--messaging-mode <mode>` | [OPTIONAL] Set how Teams delivers messages: socket or http |
| `--scopes <scopes>` | [OPTIONAL] Set bot scopes (comma-separated: personal,team,groupChat,copilot) |
| `--name <name>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the app short name (max 30 chars) |
| `--long-name <name>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the app long name (max 100 chars) |
| `--short-description <desc>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the short description (max 80 chars) |
| `--long-description <desc>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the long description (max 4000 chars) |
| `--developer <name>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the developer name |
| `--website <url>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the website URL (HTTPS required) |
| `--privacy-url <url>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the privacy policy URL (HTTPS required) |
| `--terms-url <url>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the terms of use URL (HTTPS required) |
| `--color-icon <path>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the color icon (192x192 PNG) |
| `--outline-icon <path>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the outline icon (32x32 PNG) |
| `--web-app-info-id <id>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the webApplicationInfo client ID |
| `--web-app-info-resource <uri>` | [OPTIONAL] Set the webApplicationInfo resource URI (max 100 chars) |
| `--json` | [OPTIONAL] Output as JSON |
<!-- AUTOGENERATED:END -->

## Details

Updates app properties in both TDP and (for endpoint changes on Azure bots) via `az` CLI.

### Interactive vs Scripted

- **No flags, no appId** — interactive mode: app picker, then an update menu for each property
- **With flags** — scripted mode: applies changes directly without prompts

### Endpoint Updates

When you change the endpoint, teams also updates the `validDomains` array in the manifest to include the new endpoint's domain. For Azure bots, the endpoint is updated via `az bot update`.

### Messaging Mode

Choose **Messaging mode** in the interactive update menu, or set it explicitly:

```bash
teams app update <appId> --messaging-mode socket
teams app update <appId> --messaging-mode http --endpoint https://mybot.azurewebsites.net/api/messages
```

Both Teams-managed and Azure bots support messaging-mode changes. Mode changes preserve the existing callback URL and message-notification settings. When switching to HTTP with `--endpoint`, the endpoint is updated before socket mode is disabled. `--endpoint` alone does not change the messaging mode.

`--messaging-mode socket` cannot be combined with `--endpoint`. To switch to HTTP while keeping an existing endpoint:

```bash
teams app update <appId> --messaging-mode http
```

If no endpoint is configured, the CLI warns that one is needed. HTTP delivery cannot work until a public HTTPS endpoint is set. For Azure bots, setting an endpoint requires Azure CLI to be installed and logged in; changing only the messaging mode does not.

Restart your Teams SDK application after changing the mode. Socket mode is currently available only for new bots.

#### JSON Output

For scripted updates:

```bash
teams app update <appId> --messaging-mode socket --json
```

`updated.socketMode` reports the requested mode (`true` for sockets, `false` for HTTP). Follow-up fields are included only when `true`:

| Field | Follow-up |
|-------|-----------|
| `needsRestart` | Restart the running Teams SDK application because the mode changed. |
| `needsEndpoint` | Set a messaging endpoint before using HTTP delivery. |
| `needsReinstall` | Reinstall the app in Teams after the manifest version changed, for example when adding an endpoint domain. |

Repeating a request for the already-configured mode does not include `needsRestart`. For Azure bots, `needsEndpoint` is only reported when the CLI can read the endpoint through Azure CLI; its absence is not proof that an endpoint is configured. Verify with [app get](./get) and [app doctor](./doctor).

### Examples

Update the endpoint:

```bash
teams app update <appId> --endpoint https://mybot.azurewebsites.net/api/messages
```

Update multiple properties at once:

```bash
teams app update <appId> --name "New Name" --version "2.0.0" --developer "My Team"
```

### Scopes

Update which scopes the bot supports. In interactive mode, select "Scopes" from the update menu. In scripted mode, use `--scopes`:

```bash
teams app update <appId> --scopes personal,team,copilot
```

Selecting **copilot** automatically adds the `copilotAgents.customEngineAgents` block to the manifest and ensures **personal** is included. Removing **copilot** removes the `copilotAgents` block.

Scope updates also keep the built-in personal tabs in sync: enabling **personal** adds **Chat** and **About** if missing; disabling it removes **Chat**, and removes **About** only if no other tabs remain. Whenever the resulting scopes include **personal** (including via **copilot**), a missing **Chat** tab is added first to match Teams' implicit Chat-first order. An explicitly positioned **Chat** tab keeps its position. Custom tabs and their relative order are preserved. Existing `supportsChannelFeatures` declarations are unchanged.

### webApplicationInfo (SSO)

Set the `webApplicationInfo` fields used for SSO and app identity:

```bash
teams app update <appId> --web-app-info-id <client-id> --web-app-info-resource "api://botid-<client-id>"
```

### Scopes

Update which scopes the bot supports. In interactive mode, select "Scopes" from the update menu. In scripted mode, use `--scopes`:

```bash
teams app update <appId> --scopes personal,team,copilot
```

Selecting **copilot** automatically adds the `copilotAgents.customEngineAgents` block to the manifest and ensures **personal** is included. Removing **copilot** removes the `copilotAgents` block.
